entries.q: How do I get a quote?
entries.a: Quotes are free. Message us on WhatsApp or call (813) 644-6120: we compare 30+ insurance companies and give you options. Price depends on your profile, your vehicle or property and the coverage you choose, so an agent will confirm it for you.

entries.q: Which companies do you work with?
entries.a: We are an independent agency: we compare 30+ insurance companies — such as Progressive, GEICO, National General, Kemper, Heritage or Universal Property — to find your best option.

entries.q: What auto insurance options do you have?
entries.a: We offer three levels — PIP (legal minimum), Basic and Full Cover — plus Non-Owner, high-risk, classic cars, recreational vehicles, senior driver programs and SR-22 & FR-44 filings. See auto insurance.

entries.q: What is the minimum insurance in Florida?
entries.a: In Florida every registered vehicle must be continuously insured, even when it isn’t driven. The legal minimum is $10,000 PIP + $10,000 Property Damage Liability (PDL). See coverage levels.
PIP (Personal Injury Protection) pays 80% of your medical expenses and part of your lost wages if you are injured in an accident, no matter who was at fault, up to $10,000. It is required in Florida.

“Full Cover” is the common name for a policy that includes Collision and Comprehensive on top of liability. Collision pays to repair your car after a crash; Comprehensive covers theft, vandalism, fire, flood, hail or falling trees. Ideal for new, financed or leased cars.

entries.q: What are BIL, PDL and UM?
entries.a: PDL pays for damage you cause to someone else’s property (required, $10,000 minimum). BIL pays for injuries you cause to others when you are at fault — highly recommended and required with SR-22 and FR-44. UM protects you if you are hit by someone with no or not enough insurance.
Non-Owner insurance covers you when you drive a borrowed or rented vehicle. It is ideal if you need to file an SR-22 or FR-44 and don’t have a vehicle in your name. Learn more.

An SR-22 is not insurance: it is a certificate your insurer files with the State of Florida to prove you carry the minimum required coverage ($10,000 per person / $20,000 per accident bodily injury + $10,000 property damage). It is required after serious violations and usually lasts 3 years. We handle the filing for you. See SR-22 & FR-44.

An FR-44 is similar to an SR-22 but with much higher limits: $100,000 per person / $300,000 per accident bodily injury + $50,000 property damage. It is required after a DUI conviction and usually lasts 3 years. We help you with the entire filing.

entries.q: Can I get insured with tickets or accidents?
entries.a: Yes. We offer high-risk coverage for drivers with tickets, accidents, a suspended license, little experience or a DUI conviction. We help you find a policy even if other insurers turned you down.
Yes. We offer agreed value policies: you and the insurer set your car’s value up front, and if there is a loss you receive that amount — not the depreciated market value.

entries.q: Do you insure boats, motorcycles or RVs?
entries.a: Yes. We insure your motorhome (RV), travel trailer, motorcycle, boat or jet ski so you can enjoy weekends and vacations with total peace of mind.

entries.q: Do you have programs for senior drivers?
entries.a: Yes. We have programs designed for senior drivers, with adjusted rates and benefits for those who drive fewer miles per year.

entries.q: What insurance do you have for businesses?
entries.a: For businesses we offer General Liability, Workers’ Compensation, Commercial Auto and Commercial Umbrella, plus trucking and transport coverage. See commercial insurance.

Workers’ Compensation pays medical costs and part of the wages of employees injured or made ill by their work. In Florida it is required for construction businesses with 1 or more employees and for all other businesses with 4 or more employees.

entries.q: What is a workers’ comp exemption?
entries.a: Some business owners and corporate officers can apply to the State of Florida for an exemption certificate so they don’t have to cover themselves. We help you see if you qualify and set up coverage for your employees if needed.
Commercial Auto insures the cars, vans and pickups your business uses for work. It covers accidents, injuries to others and damage to your vehicles — something a personal auto policy does not cover.

entries.q: What coverage do you have for trucks?
entries.a: For trucking we offer Primary Liability, Physical Damage, Motor Truck Cargo, Non-Trucking / Bobtail and General Liability for your premises. See trucking coverage.
Motor Truck Cargo protects you if the freight you haul is damaged, lost or ruined during the trip.

entries.q: What is bobtail or non-trucking liability?
entries.a: If you are an independent trucker leased to a company, Non-Trucking Liability (Bobtail) protects you outside of dispatch: when you drive your truck without a load or off duty.
Homeowners Insurance covers your home’s structure, your personal belongings, liability and medical costs if someone has an accident on your property. See home insurance.
No — a standard home policy does not cover flood damage. We offer specialized Flood Insurance policies to protect your property against heavy rain and hurricanes in Tampa.

Yes. Renters Insurance covers your belongings inside your apartment or house against theft, fire or water damage, plus your liability if someone gets hurt in your home. Your landlord insures the building, not your things.
A Personal Umbrella policy covers the “gaps” and costly lawsuits that go beyond the limits of your auto or home policies. There is also a commercial version for businesses.
Yes. Mobile and manufactured homes need different protection, and we offer affordable, specialized options to insure them in Tampa.
